name: Fidelity Jones
label: Dischord
lede: Two Beefeater refugees started a band with the people they lived with, spent two years stretching punk into stranger shapes, quit in 1990, and came back in 2023 after a podcast got them talking about old cover songs.

eras.title: A band starts in a group house
eras.text: Beefeater had brought funk and jazz into Revolution Summer. When it ended, singer Tomas Squip and bassist Dug E. Bird didn't go far: they started over with their housemates at the Positive Force house, home base of the scene's activist collective.

years.cap: Tomas Squip at Fidelity Jones' first show, the Wilson Center, March 1988
years.h: Beefeater's singer and bassist start over in a house full of activists
years.p: [[Tomas Squip|273702be-180d-487a-9238-2154aea60b92]] and Dug E. Bird form Fidelity Jones with housemates Maria Jones and drummer [[Jerry Busher|59c39d46-efd2-4fa0-912e-93ead7a4ab97]], at the Positive Force house.
years.xp: The first show was at the Wilson Center in March 1988, according to a scrapbook note in the Positive Force DC archive.

years.h: Maria Jones leaves to drum for Holy Rollers
years.p: She'd recorded two songs with the original line-up. Then she took the drum seat in [[Holy Rollers|d8e0e0b1-8cd9-40c7-b413-71cfcaa90547]].

eras.title: Two records and a clean exit
eras.text: Dischord's history says Fidelity Jones kept pushing the musical envelope of punk through a hard stretch for the scene, and reached the eclectic sound they'd wanted from the start. The Piltdown Lad EP and the Venus on Lovely single are what they left behind before calling it in spring 1990.

years.h: Andy Charneco arrives from White Boy and On Beyond Zebra
years.p: Andy Charneco joins on guitar, bringing time in two of the city's stranger bands.

years.cap: Dug E. Bird at Fidelity Jones' first show, Wilson Center, March 1988
years.h: A 1988 session finally surfaces on State of the Union
years.p: The original four, Maria Jones included, cut Pilate and Blood Stone Burn in 1988. Dischord 032 lands in 1989 next to [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]], [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] and [[Ignition|3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61]].

years.h: Piltdown Lad, six songs from Inner Ear
years.p: Dischord 041. The production credit reads "Andy & Fidelity Jones."

years.h: Venus on Lovely goes to Bias Studios
years.p: Dischord 047 has two songs, Venus on Lovely and Destructor. Nothing new follows until Magdeburg Lad in 2024.

years.cap: Fidelity Jones in a 1990 Dischord ad listing Dischord 047 and 041
years.h: Spring 1990, and Fidelity Jones is done
years.p: Dischord dates the band from spring 1988 to spring 1990, two years almost to the season.

eras.title: One drummer goes far, then a podcast calls
eras.text: Jerry Busher went furthest, from the Positive Force house to Fugazi's stage. Three decades on, a podcast interview put the last Fidelity Jones line-up back in a room.

years.h: Jerry Busher goes from Fugazi's crew to Fugazi's records
years.p: A Fugazi roadie through the '90s, he ends up playing extra drums, percussion and trumpet live with the band, and appears on The Argument and Furniture. The same year he starts [[French Toast|f9e0402f-c675-46d9-985f-07001bba6480]].
years.xp: Busher kept going: [[Deathfix|db0e5c06-c091-46d4-bd42-5ba2ee299123]] from 2013, and drums and percussion with [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]] in 2023 and 2024, per Wikipedia. His list of bands also runs through [[The Evens|3a3b3e5d-2d28-4108-875e-30686d2710e8]], [[Beauty Pill|976b28a1-dd68-4c43-ba08-ba15b58963b2]] and [[Blonde Redhead|6821bf3f-5d5b-4b0f-8fa4-79d2ab2d9219]].

years.h: A podcast chat turns into Magdeburg Lad
years.p: A 2023 podcast interview reunited Squip, Bird, Busher and Charneco, and talk of their old live covers became a studio booking. The digital-only EP, Dischord 198.5, followed in April 2024.
years.xp:
Two years in the making, it has two covers, one old original they never recorded, and one new song, JOY. The title echoes their 1989 debut EP, Piltdown Lad.

The band says it isn't a one-off. Fidelity Jones, per its Bandcamp and Dischord's announcement, will remain an ongoing recording entity with more music planned.
